Any two letters, the nine pairings the studies hold, and how the letters link to each other and to the Gospels.
Choose any two of the twenty-one. Each ribbon joins a passage in one to a passage in the other, where readers link them most strongly; click one to read both.
All the side-by-side pairings from the collections, in one place.

Thirty-one passages that run in parallel, paired from reading both letters and checked against Easton's list. Each weight is the number of distinct content words (by Strong's number, leaving out the commonest words) the two passages share in the Textus Receptus, so it measures shared vocabulary, not shared ideas. Other measures differ: ISBE finds 78 of Ephesians' 155 verses in Colossians "in varying degrees of identity"; Easton, quoting an older writer, counts about forty-two parallels. The household code (wives, husbands, children, fathers, servants, masters) runs in the same order in both. Ephesians 5:22–6:9 Colossians 3:18–4:1 [19]
